text:
maria_cs: Heads-up — ACME hosted account just triggered a spend anomaly. Commit is 1.2M tokens/month, current cycle shows ~1.35M and there was a 180k-token spike between 02:00-03:00 UTC. Anyone digging in?
spend-alert-bot: Alert: spend_spike_high for account=acme-corp · severity=warning · link=https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/ALRT-1132 · details=+180k tokens in 1hr · triggered_at=1754367840
ajay_reps: Noted. Who owns the integration that does bulk ingestion for ACME? Could be a pipeline re-run on their side. @sasha_csm any recent enablement work?
ken_engineering: I'll check model/route routing. Could be a fallback to a cheaper (but higher-token) model causing regen loops. Quick check on recent 5xxs?
sasha_csm: We did a demo yesterday for the onboarding team but nothing that should cause continuous calls. Reaching out to ACME AM to confirm if they ran batch processing.
maria_cs: I pulled a short query against the usage view:
```
SELECT hour, SUM(tokens) as tokens
FROM usage.events
WHERE account_id='acme-corp' AND day='2026-03-20'
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour;
```
Result: hour 02:00 => 180,214 tokens (baseline 20k/h).
billing-bot: Billing note: projected monthly burn with current trajectory = 1.78M tokens (~$X, exceeds committed tier). Auto-notify threshold crossed.
ken_engineering: No 5xx surge in that window in our logs, but I see a flurry of short streaming sessions with high completion length. Possibly prompt template loop. Can someone paste recent content or example request IDs?
sasha_csm: ACME AM replied: they kicked off a backfill for an embedding reindex job at 01:45 UTC. That might align. Reindex uses batch calls to the hosted API. Will confirm if they respected rate limits.
ajay_reps: Ok — likely non-incident; it's operational behavior. Actionables: 1) ACME to confirm backfill size & rate 2) CS to throttle with guidance + suggested batching settings 3) Eng to verify model routing didn't amplify tokens 4) Finance to note potential commit breach risk.
maria_cs: I'll file CS ticket and send suggested throttling snippet to ACME (limit concurrency + smaller seq lengths). Tagging ticket CS-912.
sasha_csm: Sent message to AM with recommended settings and temporary soft cap suggestion. They acknowledged. :thumbsup:
ken_engineering: We pulled call traces for the busiest request IDs and added a short guard to avoid regen loops. No further infra action needed now.
maria_cs: Closing loop: anomaly flagged -> root cause likely customer-initiated backfill -> CS guided throttle -> finance notified for commit uplift discussion. Will revisit next weekly check-in; marking resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
